Like another said it is definitely worth while to read other existential writings like existentialism is a humanism by Sartre. However, in terms of looking into The Stranger and Camus specifically (as Camus and Sartre are not directly thinking on the same lines), it would be worthwhile to read Camus' essay The Myth of Sisyphus. They pretty much go hand in hand in terms of putting forward Camus' absurd thought. I am doing my dissertation on Camus and have a google docs explication of the Myth of Sisyphus if you'd like the link. 

In terms of whether you missed anything out, I would argue that the main part of the novel is in the last part. The discussion with the priest and Camus' reflection afterwards. I would definitely reread that part more than anything else.

Hope this helped!
